newsitem.title: USA: UAW sets Sunday night strike deadline for GM.
newsitem.headline: UAW sets Sunday night strike deadline for GM.

text.p: The United Auto Workers union said on Friday it set a Sunday night strike deadline at General Motors Corp. in a move to pressure the automaker for an agreement on a new U.S. labour contract.
UAW President Stephen Yokich said in a statment that negotiators were not optimistic that a new contract could be reached by the deadline of 11:59 p.m. EST Sunday 0459 GMT Monday.
Yokich did not say whether the union will actually strike, but said the UAW notified GM that it will terminate its extended 1993 contract with the automaker if no deal is reached by the deadline.
"UAW members have been advised to continue to work unless notified by their local union," Yokich said.

"The UAW bargaining team will continue to make serious efforts to achieve a new agreement. While we are not optimistic, we remain hopeful that this can be accomplished prior to the expiration of the current contract at 11:59 p.m. on Sunday," he added.

The move comes just three days after GM settled a 20-day strike with the Canadian Auto Workers union that caused parts shortages that are still forcing the world's largest automaker to shut down some of its U.S. assembly plants.
